# Microsoft Entra ID — Identity Telemetry Emission

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Detail |
|---|---|
| Role | **Security Administrator** on the Entra tenant — required to create or edit any diagnostic setting ([log options reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/monitoring-health/concept-diagnostic-settings-logs-options)) |
| Additional role | **Attribute Log Administrator** *plus* Security Administrator, if routing `CustomSecurityAttributeAuditLogs` |
| Destination | Log Analytics workspace, Event Hubs namespace, or storage account — **must exist before** the diagnostic setting is created |
| License | `MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs` requires Entra ID **P1 or P2** ([data retention](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/monitoring-health/reference-reports-data-retention#how-long-does-microsoft-entra-id-store-the-data)) |
| Tenancy | The subscription and Event Hubs namespace must be associated with the same Entra tenant whose logs you are streaming |

## The log categories

These are every category Entra diagnostic settings can route, with the
Log Analytics table each lands in. Categories marked **Core** carry the
AU-2 / AU-3 / AU-12 evidence stream and should be enabled in every federal
tenant regardless of feature adoption.

| Category | Log Analytics table | Tier | What it captures |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AuditLogs` | `AuditLogs` | **Core** | Directory changes — users, groups, apps, licenses, roles, policy |
| `SignInLogs` | `SigninLogs` | **Core** | Interactive user sign-ins (username/password, MFA challenge) |
| `NonInteractiveUserSignInLogs` | `AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs` | **Core** | Sign-ins on behalf of a user by a client app using a token or code |
| `ServicePrincipalSignInLogs` | `AADServicePrincipalSignInLogs` | **Core** | App / service-principal authentication via certificate or client secret |
| `ManagedIdentitySignInLogs` | `AADManagedIdentitySignInLogs` | **Core** | Managed-identity authentication where Azure holds the secret |
| `ProvisioningLogs` | `AADProvisioningLogs` | **Core** | Users, groups, roles provisioned by the Entra provisioning service |
| `MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs` | `MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs` | **Core** | Every HTTP request against tenant resources through the Graph API |
| `RiskyUsers` | `AADRiskyUsers` | High value | ID Protection — users assessed as at risk |
| `UserRiskEvents` | `AADUserRiskEvents` | High value | ID Protection — individual risk detections |
| `RiskyServicePrincipals` | `AADRiskyServicePrincipals` | High value | ID Protection — risky workload identities |
| `ServicePrincipalRiskEvents` | `AADServicePrincipalRiskEvents` | High value | ID Protection — workload-identity risk detections |
| `ADFSSignInLogs` | `ADFSSignInLogs` | Conditional | AD FS application sign-in activity — required while federation persists |
| `CustomSecurityAttributeAuditLogs` | `CustomSecurityAttributeAuditLogs` | Conditional | Changes to custom security attributes |
| `RiskyAgents` | `RiskyAgents` | Conditional | ID Protection — agent identities assessed as risky |
| `AgentRiskEvents` | `AgentRiskEvents` | Conditional | ID Protection — agent risk detections |
| `NetworkAccessTrafficLogs` | `NetworkAccessTraffic` | Conditional | Global Secure Access traffic — no data unless GSA is deployed |
| `RemoteNetworkHealthLogs` | `RemoteNetworkHealthLogs` | Conditional | Global Secure Access remote-network health |
| `EnrichedOffice365AuditLogs` | `EnrichedMicrosoft365AuditLogs` | Conditional | GSA-enriched M365 logs — requires GSA *and* enrichment enabled |
| `MicrosoftServicePrincipalSignInLogs` | — | **Not recommended** | First-party Microsoft service-to-service auth (preview) |

Category names and behavior are from
[What are the identity logs you can stream to an endpoint?](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/monitoring-health/concept-diagnostic-settings-logs-options);
table names from the
[Microsoft Entra ID data connector reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/sentinel/connect-azure-active-directory#microsoft-entra-id-data-connector-data-types)
and the [ID Protection export guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/id-protection/howto-export-risk-data#log-analytics).

::: {.callout-tip}
## Confirm table names against your own workspace

Most — not all — Entra tables carry an `AAD` prefix, and the mapping is not
mechanical (`SignInLogs` → `SigninLogs` with a lowercase `i`;
`EnrichedOffice365AuditLogs` → `EnrichedMicrosoft365AuditLogs`). Before
committing detection rules or retention policy that name a table, confirm it
resolves in the target workspace. The verification query in
[§Verify emission](#verify-emission) does this for the seven core tables.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## Do not enable `MicrosoftServicePrincipalSignInLogs`

Microsoft's own guidance is that these logs "are not necessary for most
customers as they are complex and generate a high volume of data," that the
data "is not essential for security investigations," and that Microsoft
"strongly advise[s] against taking actions such as disabling applications
based on this data, as doing so could cause misconfigurations and potential
adverse effects such as tenant lock-out"
([log options reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/monitoring-health/concept-diagnostic-settings-logs-options)).

The ingestion cost is real and the analytic value is negative. Leave it off.
:::

### Why the four sign-in categories are not optional

`SignInLogs` alone covers interactive human sign-ins. It does not cover the
client app refreshing a token on a user's behalf, the service principal
authenticating with a client secret, or the managed identity pulling from Key
Vault. Those are `NonInteractiveUserSignInLogs`,
`ServicePrincipalSignInLogs`, and `ManagedIdentitySignInLogs` respectively.

This is the exact failure the repo's own boundary probe was written to catch —
symptom #1, "invisible non-interactive / service-principal / managed-identity
sign-in activity," validated by
[`01-entra-diagnostic-completeness.kql`](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/adapters/modernization/gcc_boundary_probe/queries/01-entra-diagnostic-completeness.kql).
A tenant with only `SignInLogs` enabled is blind to every non-human
authentication in the estate while appearing, on the sign-ins blade, to be
fully instrumented.

## Path A — Portal

The click-path, for tenants where configuration is a one-time manual act:

1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com)
   as at least **Security Administrator**.
2. Browse to **Entra ID** → **Monitoring & health** → **Diagnostic settings**.
   (**Export Settings** on the **Audit Logs** or **Sign-ins** blade reaches
   the same place.)
3. Select **+ Add diagnostic setting**.
4. Enter a **Diagnostic setting name**. This cannot be changed later — pick
   something an assessor will recognize, e.g. `uiao-siem-emission-core`.
5. Under **Logs**, check every category from the **Core** tier above, plus the
   **High value** tier if ID Protection is licensed.
6. Under **Destination details**, select **Send to Log Analytics workspace**
   (and/or **Stream to an event hub** for a third-party SIEM), then choose the
   subscription and target.
7. **Save**.

Data begins appearing at the destination after roughly **15 minutes**
([configure diagnostic settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/monitoring-health/howto-configure-diagnostic-settings#select-the-logs-and-destination)).

::: {.callout-note}
## The portal is fine for the first tenant and wrong for the fleet

A portal-configured diagnostic setting has no source of truth, no review
trail, and no drift detection — it is a click somebody made once. FedRAMP
**KSI-MLA-EVC** requires that the configuration of machine-based information
resources "especially infrastructure as code, is persistently evaluated and
tested." Use Path B or C for anything that has to survive an assessment.
:::

## Path B — Tenant-scope ARM / Bicep

Entra diagnostic settings are the ARM resource type
`microsoft.aadiam/diagnosticSettings`, API version `2017-04-01`, and they
deploy at **tenant scope**
([resource reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/templates/microsoft.aadiam/2017-04-01/diagnosticsettings)).

```bicep
// entra-diagnostics.bicep
// Deploy with: az deployment tenant create --location <region> \
//   --template-file entra-diagnostics.bicep \
//   --parameters workspaceId=<log-analytics-resource-id>
targetScope = 'tenant'

@description('Full ARM resource ID of the destination Log Analytics workspace.')
param workspaceId string

@description('Diagnostic setting name. Immutable once created.')
param settingName string = 'uiao-siem-emission-core'

var coreCategories = [
  'AuditLogs'
  'SignInLogs'
  'NonInteractiveUserSignInLogs'
  'ServicePrincipalSignInLogs'
  'ManagedIdentitySignInLogs'
  'ProvisioningLogs'
  'MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs'
  'RiskyUsers'
  'UserRiskEvents'
  'RiskyServicePrincipals'
  'ServicePrincipalRiskEvents'
]

resource entraDiagnostics 'microsoft.aadiam/diagnosticSettings@2017-04-01' = {
  name: settingName
  properties: {
    workspaceId: workspaceId
    logs: [for category in coreCategories: {
      category: category
      enabled: true
      // retentionPolicy is honored only for storage-account destinations.
      // Log Analytics retention is set per-table — see page 4.
      retentionPolicy: {
        days: 0
        enabled: false
      }
    }]
  }
}
```

::: {.callout-important}
## `retentionPolicy` here does nothing for Log Analytics

The `retentionPolicy` block on a diagnostic setting is "used for storage
accounts only"
([Azure Monitor REST API reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/data-factory/monitor-logs-rest#enable-diagnostic-logs-via-the-monitor-rest-api)).
Setting `days: 3650` here and believing you have satisfied AU-11 or M-21-31 is
a common and expensive mistake — the retention that counts is configured
per-table on the workspace. See
[Compliance crosswalk and verification](04-compliance-crosswalk.qmd#retention).
:::

## Path C — `az rest`

`az monitor diagnostic-settings create` targets resources inside a resource
group and **cannot** create an Entra tenant-scope setting. Operators who try
it hit an opaque failure. Use `az rest` against the ARM endpoint directly:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Create or update the Entra tenant diagnostic setting.
# Requires: Security Administrator on the tenant.
set -euo pipefail

SETTING_NAME="uiao-siem-emission-core"
WORKSPACE_ID="/subscriptions/${SUBSCRIPTION_ID}/resourceGroups/${RG}/providers/Microsoft.OperationalInsights/workspaces/${WORKSPACE}"

CATEGORIES=(
  AuditLogs SignInLogs NonInteractiveUserSignInLogs
  ServicePrincipalSignInLogs ManagedIdentitySignInLogs
  ProvisioningLogs MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs
  RiskyUsers UserRiskEvents
  RiskyServicePrincipals ServicePrincipalRiskEvents
)

LOGS_JSON=$(printf '%s\n' "${CATEGORIES[@]}" \
  | jq -R . | jq -s 'map({category: ., enabled: true})')

az rest --method PUT \
  --uri "https://management.azure.com/providers/microsoft.aadiam/diagnosticSettings/${SETTING_NAME}?api-version=2017-04-01" \
  --headers "Content-Type=application/json" \
  --body "$(jq -n --arg ws "$WORKSPACE_ID" --argjson logs "$LOGS_JSON" \
      '{properties: {workspaceId: $ws, logs: $logs}}')"
```

Read the current state back — this is also the supported way to discover which
categories a given tenant actually supports, since availability varies with
licensing and feature enablement:

```bash
az rest --method GET \
  --uri "https://management.azure.com/providers/microsoft.aadiam/diagnosticSettings?api-version=2017-04-01" \
  --query "value[].{name:name, workspace:properties.workspaceId, categories:properties.logs[?enabled].category}" \
  -o jsonc
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Sovereign clouds

Replace `management.azure.com` with `management.usgovcloudapi.net` for Azure
Government. Entra portal and Graph endpoints shift too — see the
[endpoint table](index.qmd#sovereign-cloud-endpoints). GCC (the current UIAO
boundary) stays on the worldwide ARM and Graph endpoints.
:::

## Microsoft Graph — targeted evidence, not the feed

Graph's `auditLogs` endpoints answer *"show me this specific thing"*. They are
the wrong tool for continuous ingestion, and Microsoft says so directly: the
API "isn't designed for pulling large amounts of activity data," which "might
lead to issues with pagination and performance"
([analyze activity logs with Graph](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/monitoring-health/howto-analyze-activity-logs-with-microsoft-graph#access-reports-using-microsoft-graph-explorer)).

### Endpoints

| Endpoint | Returns |
|---|---|
| `GET /v1.0/auditLogs/directoryAudits` | Directory change history — role grants, app consent, password resets, group management ([reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/directoryaudit-list?view=graph-rest-1.0)) |
| `GET /v1.0/auditLogs/signIns` | Interactive, non-interactive, service-principal, and managed-identity sign-ins ([reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/signin-list?view=graph-rest-1.0#permissions)) |
| `GET /v1.0/auditLogs/provisioning` | Provisioning-service activity |
| `GET /beta/auditLogs/signUps` | Self-service sign-up activity (beta — not for production) |

### Permissions

`AuditLog.Read.All` is the least-privileged permission for both delegated and
application access on `directoryAudits` and `signIns`. `Get directoryAudit`
(single item) additionally requires `Directory.Read.All`. For delegated
access the signed-in user must hold a supporting role — **Reports Reader**,
**Security Reader**, **Security Administrator**, or **Global Reader**
depending on the endpoint.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Conditional Access data is separately gated

`appliedConditionalAccessPolicies` is **omitted** from the `signIns` response
unless the caller also holds `Policy.Read.All`,
`Policy.Read.ConditionalAccess`, or `Policy.ReadWrite.ConditionalAccess`
([signIns permissions](https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/signin-list?view=graph-rest-1.0#permissions)).

The property is dropped silently — no error, no warning. An evidence pipeline
built without one of those permissions produces sign-in records that look
complete and contain no CA evaluation data at all, which is precisely the
evidence AC-2 and AC-6 assessment turns on. This is the repo's boundary-probe
symptom #5, "CA evaluation-log incompleteness."
:::

### Example — CA failures in a bounded window

Always apply a `createdDateTime` filter; unbounded queries time out.

```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/auditLogs/signIns
  ?$filter=conditionalAccessStatus eq 'failure'
    and createdDateTime ge 2026-08-01T00:00:00Z
    and createdDateTime lt 2026-08-08T00:00:00Z
  &$top=999
Authorization: Bearer {token}
```

PowerShell equivalent, via the Graph SDK:

```powershell
Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'AuditLog.Read.All','Policy.Read.All'

Get-MgAuditLogDirectoryAudit -Filter @"
category eq 'RoleManagement' and activityDateTime gt 2026-08-01T00:00:00Z
"@ -All
```

For Azure Government, connect with `-Environment USGov` and request the
`https://graph.microsoft.us/.default` scope
([national clouds with the Graph SDKs](https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/sdks/national-clouds#examples)).

## Verify emission {#verify-emission}

Configuration succeeding is not emission succeeding. Run this against the
destination workspace 24 hours after the setting is created, and on a
schedule thereafter — every core table must return a non-zero `RecordCount`
with `LastRecord` inside the last day.

```kusto
// Entra diagnostic-setting completeness.
// Pass criterion: every row returns RecordCount > 0
// and LastRecord within the last 24h.
union withsource=TableName
    SigninLogs,
    AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs,
    AADServicePrincipalSignInLogs,
    AADManagedIdentitySignInLogs,
    AuditLogs,
    AADProvisioningLogs,
    MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs,
    AADRiskyUsers,
    AADUserRiskEvents
| summarize RecordCount = count(), LastRecord = max(TimeGenerated) by TableName
| extend Stale = LastRecord < ago(24h)
| order by Stale desc, TableName asc
```

A table that is **absent from the result entirely** has never received data —
that category was never enabled, or was enabled against a different
workspace. A table present but `Stale` means emission stopped, which is the
more dangerous condition because the historical data masks it on any query
with a wide time range.

::: {.callout-important}
## This query is canon, not an example

The substrate ships this check as
[`01-entra-diagnostic-completeness.kql`](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/adapters/modernization/gcc_boundary_probe/queries/01-entra-diagnostic-completeness.kql),
executed by the GCC Boundary Probe adapter, which emits per-symptom
`DRIFT-BOUNDARY` findings. The version above adds
`MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs` and the explicit staleness flag. Treat the
committed `.kql` as the source of truth and this page as its narrative
explanation.
:::

## Sentinel data connector

If the destination workspace is Microsoft Sentinel, the **Microsoft Entra ID**
data connector surfaces the same categories through the connector UI rather
than the Entra diagnostic-settings blade. They write to the same tables;
enabling both does not duplicate data. Connector setup, expected EPS at
5,000 users, and the detection rules built on these tables are covered in
[Vol III Book 06 §Connector: Entra ID](../../orgcomp-series/Vol_III_Book_06_OrgComp_SIEM_XDR_Detection.qmd).

## What this page does not cover

Entra diagnostic settings emit **identity** events. They do not emit Azure
resource activity (see [Azure platform](02-azure-platform.qmd)) and they do
not emit the Microsoft 365 unified audit log (see
[M365 unified audit](03-m365-unified-audit.qmd)). Nor do they recover the
26 telemetry signals the FedRAMP Moderate boundary blocks outright — that
accounting is in
[Event Logging Under the GCC-Moderate Boundary](../../whitepapers/event-logging-fedramp-boundary-limitations.qmd).
